articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google A new sale to coincide with Black Friday has seen Capcom's Resident Evil Requiem fall to its lowest price yet. Since launching near the start of this yea r, the latest Resident Evil game has been discounted a handful of times for both its digital and physical editions. However, many of these past sales for the game have never seen it fall much beneath the $40 threshold, with digital sales barely dipping past $50. Luckily, for those who have continued to hold off on picking up Resident Evil Requiem for a better deal, a new offer has now gone live.

Over at Walmart , Resident Evil Requiem has seen its price slashed all the way down to $30. This represents the lowest amount that RE Requiem has ever been sold for, and is a discount of roughly $40 off of its normal value. Previously, Requiem's lowest amount before this deal was $39.99, which means that this new sale surpasses its previous best discount by a decent margin.

The only downside with this sale for Resident Evil Requiem , however, is that it's not available for all platforms. Instead, this discount only applies to the version of the game on PS5. While many are likely looking to play RE Requiem on PS5 in the first place, it's still a bummer for those who are instead trying to get a discount on the Xbox and Nintendo Switch 2 editions of the game.

Looking ahead, there's a good chance that this sale for Resident Evil Requiem might not be topped before Christmas rolls around. Many other retailers have also cut the price of Requiem to coincide with Black Friday, but none other than Walmart has brought the game all the way down to $30. The game's digital iteration on the PS Store also hasn't seen its value dropped whatsoever for PlayStation's Black Friday deals, as it remains at its usual retail price. With this in mind, it seems clear that many marketplaces aren't willing to substantially cut the price of Resident Evil Requiem just yet, which makes this ongoing deal at Walmart stand out that much more.

How do you feel about this new Black Friday sale for Resident Evil Requiem ? If you don't already own the game for yourself, is this new offer going to get you to finally pull the trigger? Be sure to let me know down in the comments section.

articles.title: Top MS NOW Hosts Sign Letter Urging Versant to Ink Deal With Writers Guild East Members (Exclusive)
articles.summary: Rachel Maddow, Chris Hayes, Jen Psaki and Lawrence O'Donnell are among the hosts that have signed the letter, which calls on the company to cut a deal 'without division or delay.'
articles.content:
Some of MS NOW 's top on-air hosts and journalists have signed an open letter calling on parent company Versant to come to terms on a new collective bargaining agreement with employees who are members of the Writers Guild of America East.

The current contract with the union is set to expire Dec. 3.

The letter, which was delivered to management at the bargaining table, begins: "As hosts and guests of MS NOW programs, we stand in solidarity with the MS NOW Union as they fight for a contract that addresses inflation, AI protections, and retirement security. As one of the most trusted names in news, we are proud of our programming and the MS NOW producers that make it possible."

Among the signers of the letter are Rachel Maddow, Jen Psaki, Chris Hayes, Lawrence O'Donnell, Ali Velshi, Alicia Menendez, Symone Sanders Townsend, Jacob Soboroff, Chris Jansing, and Katie Phang.

"We're disappointed that Versant Media's decision makers expect unit members to work extra hours creating new digital content, without treating it as extra work or paying for it. On top of that, we are disappointed that Versant Media will not agree to the Union's demands for annual and minimum wage increases that keep pace with inflation," the letter continues. "We are calling on the Company to agree to a quick and fair process to recognize all employees' rightful place in the MS NOW Union without division or delay. Additionally, we call on the Company to agree to a contract that will protect wages, benefits, and security at work."

In addition to cutting a new deal with the 300 or so existing WGAE members, the union is also seeking union recognition for another 50 employees across Digital, Audio and Longform, Newsgathering, Planning, and the DC Bureau.

The first contract with what was then MSNBC was ratified in 2023, and included annual pay increases and policies around overnight and extra work. The MSNBC union was formed in 2021. At the time of that first contract, the WGAE leaned on celebrity writer support from the likes of Tina Fey, David Simon and Adam McKay to apply pressure on NBCUniversal to cut a deal.

The letter from top talent however ramps up pressure on Versant to cut a deal with the WGAE, given the high-profile of the letter's signees and the left-leaning politics of the channel's talent and audience.

The WGAE has a robust membership across broadcast and cable news, including groups at ABC News, CBS News, the NBC promo writers, and stations like CBS 2, WNET, Fox 5 and 1010 WINS.

TalkShopLive , the live commerce and entertainment platform for signed music, books and celebrity merch is expanding to TikTok Shop ahead of the Black Friday shopping season .

The new partnership will see TalkShopLive’s exclusive content and inventory of products available to view and purchase on TikTok, opening up another channel for fans to discover and shop official releases straight from the stars. TalkShopLive has carved out a distinctive position in entertainment commerce, by helping artists, authors and entertainment companies turn new releases into direct-to-fan shopping experiences, often built around exclusive signed vinyl, autographed books, limited-edition albums and celebrity collectibles. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Recent livestreams on TalkShopLive have included Andy Cohen, promoting his new “ Bravo Scrapbook ” compendium, while Kenny Chesney and John Legend stopped by individually to offer signed copies of their new albums. Fans can also shop limited-edition merch on the TalkShopLive website directly, with signed copies of Bunnie XO’s memoir “ Stripped Down: Unfiltered and Unapologetic ,” and Jimmy Fallon’s children’s book, “ Papa Doesn’t Do Anything! (But Love You) ” among the current bestsellers.

While much of the attention in social commerce has focused on TikTok Shop, Whatnot and eBay, TalkShopLive has quietly built a formidable shoppable entertainment marketplace to the stars, becoming an important part of first-week sales strategies for major record labels, book publishers and some of the biggest names in entertainment. Now, TalkShopLive is tapping into the TikTok audience to continue to grow its presence and reach.

“We’ve built TalkShopLive around something that has always been incredibly powerful in entertainment: the connection between talent and their fans,” says Bryan Moore, CEO and co-founder of TalkShopLive. “From the biggest names in music to bestselling authors and cultural icons, we’ve created a shoppable platform where exclusive releases and signed merchandise have become an important part of how entertainment is launched and sold. Expanding to TikTok Shop gives our partners another turnkey opportunity to maximize the reach of their shoppable content and exclusive products, connect with more fans and drive meaningful sales.”

The move comes as TikTok Shop continues to reshape online shopping and product discovery, while demand for signed merchandise and exclusive entertainment collectibles creates new opportunities for artists, labels and publishers to connect directly with consumers.

Unlike traditional resale marketplaces, TalkShopLive has built its business around direct relationships with artists, record labels and book publishers, giving fans access to officially sourced signed merchandise and exclusive releases rather than relying on the secondary resale market.

The TikTok expansion also builds on TalkShopLive’s existing cross-platform commerce presence, with shoppable experiences currently across Meta’s Facebook and Instagram platforms, as well as YouTube . The company’s proprietary distributed video commerce technology also powers livestream shopping for major retailers, including Walmart’s Walmart Live, and supports the distribution of Amazon Live programming across additional media properties.

Celebrities who have worked with TalkShopLive, meantime, have included everyone from Martha Stewart and Oprah, to Garth Brooks and Paul McCartney.

articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Netflix has acquired the exclusive streaming rights to one of the most enigmatic power fantasies and love stories, beginning in January 2027. The giant streaming platform has gained significant access to the anime world over the past few years, bringing many popular anime to its platform. At the same time, Netflix has also secured the rights to several exclusive anime. 2027 looks set to continue this trend, with one of the latest Winter 2027 anime joining another exclusive, Sakamoto Days , being Bride of the Barrier Master .

The anime was first announced in August 2025, with a Winter 2027 release window. Now, with the Winter season fast approaching, its release date has finally been revealed, with the series arriving exclusively on Netflix on January 6. It is an exciting announcement, as the romantic fantasy manga and light novel series has built a dedicated fan base eager to see its vibrant world brought to life through an anime adaptation and experience its romantic banter. The staff behind the anime's production and the latest teaser have also offered promising signs of what Netflix's exclusive title has in store.

Bride of the Barrier Master is being animated by Troyca, with Toru Kitahata serving as the director. The production also features Akari Kito as the female lead, Hana Ichise, who is known for several roles, including Nezuko in Demon Slayer and Hina Chono in Blue Box , another Netflix exclusive in international regions. Meanwhile, the male lead, Saku Ichinomiya, will be voiced by Kikunosuke Toya, another renowned voice actor in the anime industry, best known for roles such as Denji. His casting makes him a perfect fit for Saku, a rowdy character who likes to take charge.

While the production committee looks promising, with the latest visuals and teasers making the anime shine, the series' narrative is what will make it stand out even more. The fantasy series follows a neglected girl named Hana Ichise, who is believed to lack the power required of one of the protectors of the pillars that safeguard Japan. She is constantly overshadowed by her older twin sister, who possesses the necessary power and fulfills her duties. However, Hana secretly possesses immense power but refuses to use it because she wants to live a normal life. Unfortunately, fate has other plans, as her secret is eventually discovered by the young head of the clan, Saku Ichinomiya.

Saku initially pressures Hana into marrying him, which she naturally refuses. However, she is eventually forced into the marriage, as she has no other options. Thus begins Hana's new life, as her desire to live peacefully despite possessing immense power is disrupted by her marriage to the head of the clan. This adds a romantic twist to her journey, promising a series of hilarious moments and an unconventional love story that fans can immerse themselves in. Netflix has a reputation for featuring a variety of anime , and Bride of the Barrier Master 's exclusivity adds another unique title to its catalogue. It could even emerge as the platform's biggest romantic fantasy anime of 2027.

articles.title: Netflix's 'The Murder of JonBenét Ramsey' Haunting Trailer Shines Spotlight on Melissa McCarthy and Clive Owen
articles.summary: The limited series from showrunner Richard LaGravenese releases its 10 episodes in December.
articles.content:
That's the conclusion drawn by the trailer for the newest take on the infamous JonBenét Ramsey murder cold case.

Netflix's The Murder of JonBenét Ramsey , which recruited Melissa McCarthy and Clive Owen for the roles of JonBenét’s parents Patsy and John Bennett Ramsey, respectively, will get its turn to tell the enduring, unsolved mystery of JonBenét Ramsey’s murder when the limited series releases all 10 episodes on Dec. 10.

"I was fascinated by the challenge of doing something that was a murder mystery without an ending, without being solved," says showrunner Richard LaGravenese with the first look announcement, which included the trailer and new photos (below). blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Lifestyle Harrison Ford Joins Greg Berlanti, Goldie Hawn and Melissa McCarthy as Paley Gala Honorees TV Melissa McCarthy and Clive Owen Are JonBenét Ramsey's Parents in First Look at Netflix Series on Enduring True-Crime Case

There has been curiosity around how the latest screen take would handle adapting the true crime story of the devastating murder of 6-year-old Ramsey — the beauty pageant winner was found strangled in the basement of her Boulder, Colorado, family home on Dec. 26, 1996. Thirty years later, mystery around her death remains. Netflix’s recent doc Cold Case: Who Killed JonBenét Ramsey from filmmaker Joe Berlinger , in November 2024, pointed the finger at the Boulder Police Department as for why the case remains unsolved.

The trailer (below) for The Murder of JonBenét Ramsey plays out like a haunting thriller-mystery, as it traces the steps of the well-known-by-know investigation by the Boulder Police, which includes questioning Patsy and John, contaminated evidence and the case becoming a tabloid sensation. "The country is looking for an end to this story that makes sense to them," says the District Attorney Hunter, played by Shea Whigham in the trailer. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Owen and McCarthy are "unlike anything you've seen them do before," said Netflix in its marketing for the series. Owen said of the series' take, "It felt to me that if there was one thing that you could really hold onto as an anchor for the whole thing, it was the fact that it’s a tragedy. It’s not a whodunit; a little girl died.” McCarthy added, "We all forgot that these were parents and they loved their children. And one of them was taken in such an unimaginably violent, terrible way. That should be the crux of the story, and it became almost non-existent. It became like it didn’t even matter. We were just watching this exciting tale of who did it.”

The Murder of JonBenét Ramsey was greenlit back in 2024 at Paramount+ before Paramount’s takeover by Skydance. Production on the series wrapped in early 2025 under the title Unspeakable: The Murder of JonBenet Ramsey . The intent was to have it be the first installment of an anthology series , like Netflix’s Monster franchise, to examine unsolved crimes. But after Skydance took over Paramount, the series was quietly shelved. 101 Studios moved from Paramount to NBCUniversal earlier this year, following Taylor Sheridan, and the series then landed at Netflix this summer.

Here’s the logline for The Murder of JonBenét Ramsey : “The series centers on one of the most infamous unsolved murder cases in American history, and the devastating personal and public reckoning that followed the death of JonBenet Ramsey on Christmas night in 1996.” blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Rounding out the cast is Emily Mitchell in the role of JonBenét Ramsey and Angus Caldwell as her brother, Burke Ramsey. Additional cast includes a group of local and federal investigators, played by an ensemble including Garrett Hedlund, Will Patton, Whigham and Alison Pill.

Jeremy Bobb, John Billingsley, Josh Stamberg, Margo Martindale, Tzi Ma, Owen Teague, Clifton Collins Jr., Jaime Ray Newman, Rory Cochrane and Chris Bauer also star.

LaGravenese ( Behind the Candelabra, Freedom Writers, A Family Affair ) is showrunner, with Anne Sewitsky (Presumed Innocent ) as a director and executive producer. articles.title: 'The Comedy About Spies' to Open on Broadway This Spring
articles.summary: The spoof is from the same team as the slapstick comedy 'The Play That Goes Wrong.'
articles.content:
The Comedy About Spies, from the makers of The Play That Goes Wrong, is coming to Broadway this spring.

The play is set to play an 18-week engagement at the Music Box Theatre starting March 27, ahead of an April 14 opening night. The show comes to Broadway after premiering in the West End in 2025, and then returning there for a brief run this August.

The Comedy About Spies will star members of the original Mischief company, though exact members were not named. The play is written by Mischief co-founders Henry Lewis and Henry Shields and directed by Matt DiCarlo. As with their previous works, including The Play That Goes Wrong , which ran on Broadway from 2017 to 2019, the play involves a large degree of physical and slapstick comedy, with the set playing a large role.

“When a rogue British agent steals plans for a top-secret weapon, CIA and KGB spies descend on London’s Piccadilly Hotel in pursuit of the elusive file. Throw in a clueless young couple, a hapless actor angling for a part in a spy movie and enough double agents to confuse even the sharpest operative, and the result is a 1960s escapade of bungled missions, tangled identities and catastrophic miscommunication that spirals hilariously out of control,” the production description reads.

The play features set design by David Farley, costume design by Deborah Andrews, movement direction by Shelley Maxwell, lighting design by Johanna Town and sound design and composition by Jon Fiber for Jollygoodtunes.

The Comedy About Spies is produced on Broadway by Kevin McCollum ( Six, Oh, Mary!) , Kenny Wax and Stage Presence Ltd in association with Jo Danvers.

articles.title: Red Dead Redemption Movie Gets Surprising Update, With 1 Major Problem
articles.summary: GTA VI may be on everyone's mind right now, but Rockstar's previous masterpiece, Red Dead Redemption, may have captured Hollywood's attention. Though the glitz, glamour, and crime of Vice City is at the center of almost every headline right now, the Grand Theft Auto series seems pretty well confined to video games for the time […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google GTA VI may be on everyone's mind right now , but Rockstar's previous masterpiece, Red Dead Redemption , may have captured Hollywood's attention. Though the glitz, glamour, and crime of Vice City is at the center of almost every headline right now, the Grand Theft Auto series seems pretty well confined to video games for the time being. That said, Take-Two's CEO just revealed last week that if the right idea came around for a Grand Theft Auto movie or TV show, then they'd definitely consider it, but on the flip side, it seems Red Dead is way more likely, but it comes with a price tag.

According to Puck News , talk of Rockstar bringing the license to Red Dead Redemption out into the world has started to create buzz in Hollywood. The outlet reports that Rockstar and Take-Two are seeking a hefty sum, though, citing an agent who revealed: "They were throwing around a purchase price of more than $100 million minimum for licensing rights.” Given how sacred a franchise like Red Dead Redemption is to the developer and players, it's easy to see why the license would cost that much, but it could make the series prohibitively expensive.

It's worth noting that the $100 million license price, which was noted as being the "minimum," is just the cost associated with a studio grabbing the rights to develop the property into a movie or TV show. That means that if a studio decided to bite and pay up, they're already down a nine-figure sum before they've even hired a writing team to bring the project to life. On top of that, Red Dead Redemption 's period setting would command a major budget, meaning the cost for bringing this game to life as a film or show is going to cost a lot of money.

Even with that huge cost firmly established, it's still within reason to think that a studio might bite. Amazon previously plunked down a huge sum to bring The Lord of the Rings to Prime Video as a TV series, paying a quarter of a billion dollars for the TV rights alone. Since then, estimates have put the total amount Amazon has spent on The Rings of Power at over a billion dollars, when factoring in not only production and visual effects costs, but also marketing.

Considering the astronomical costs of a potential Red Dead Redemption adaptation, that's without even factoring in the uphill battle it would face with the player base of the game itself. Though the actual narrative of Red Dead Redemption games has captivated fans with how the story plays out, there's still an element of player choice that is at the heart of the titles that helped make them fan favorites. Players could choose to engage with the plot, or they could do whatever they wanted in the wilderness for hours on end. It's been the problem that has plagued video game movies for literal decades.

That said, video game adaptations have clearly entered a new era. TV shows like Fallout , The Last of Us , and Cyberpunk: Edgerunners have proven that they can work and create all-new fans who will then play the games themselves. In the end, that's the main reason for a game studio to license their title for another medium, something that even Take-Two admitted worked in their favor with the disaster of the Borderlands movie. Hopefully the same won't be said for Red Dead Redemption in a few years.

articles.title: These 3 Marvel Movies Are Required Viewing on Thanksgiving, And They're Doomsday Prep Too
articles.summary: Thanksgiving in the United States is just around the corner, and one of the most common complaints about the holiday is that there aren't many Thanksgiving movies. While there are gems like Planes, Trains and Automobiles and movies that give off a Thanksgiving vibe like Fantastic Mr. Fox, there aren't nearly as many options as […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Thanksgiving in the United States is just around the corner, and one of the most common complaints about the holiday is that there aren't many Thanksgiving movies. While there are gems like Planes, Trains and Automobiles and movies that give off a Thanksgiving vibe like Fantastic Mr. Fox , there aren't nearly as many options as there are for Halloween or Christmas.

Luckily for Marvel fans who celebrate, there are several superhero movies that perfectly give off the Thanksgiving vibe. So, here are three crowd-pleasers that you can turn on after finishing your turkey, that double as prep for Avengers: Doomsday .

Sam Raimi's 2002 Spider-Man is one of the most iconic superhero movies of all time, with it and FOX's X-Men films helping to launch the modern superhero movie craze. Unlike many of the later Spider-Man movies that become overstuffed with multiple villains and crossover superheroes, this one is fairly simple. It tells the story of how Peter Parker became Spider-Man, his relationship with Mary Jane, and his fight against Green Goblin. However, this film is also notable for featuring a scene in which Peter, Mary Jane, Aunt May, and Harry and Norman Osborne celebrate Thanksgiving together. Norman even gets chastized for attempting to dig in too early, which is probably the most relatable thing the villain does in the whole movie.

On top of that, 2002's Spider-Man could wind up being prep for Avengers: Doomsday . Tobey Maguire's Peter Parker already joined the MCU when he was brought to Earth-199999 in Spider-Man: No Way Home . While he returned to his universe at the end of the film, there are rumors that he may reappear in Doomsday . However, it will be far darker than the character's previous appearances. According to these rumors, Doomsday will open with an incursion event between Sam Raimi's Spider-Man universe and the X-Men universe, meaning that one or both of these worlds could be destroyed. We probably won't know whether Maguire is in Doomsday until the film comes out, but if things go as rumored, fans of the original trilogy may have wished he wasn't.

2025's The Fantastic Four: First Steps finally introduced Marvel's first family to the MCU, with it being one of the franchise's most stylized films yet. First Steps is easily the best Fantastic Four movie, and these iterations of the characters are near-perfect adaptations. While the film doesn't take place at Thanksgiving, it's all about family, one of the most important parts of the holiday. On top of that, the conflict of the film revolves around a feast. The Fantastic Four are tasked with stopping Galactus from eating the entire planet, and some viewers may feel like they've done just that after their Thanksgiving meals.

Now is also a great time to rewatch First Steps , as the characters will be integral to Doomsday . The film's trailers have proven that the team knew Victor von Doom before the events of Doomsday , meaning that we will undoubtedly see more of their backstory in the film. The Thunderbolts* post-credits scene already confirmed that the team will travel to Earth-199999, meaning that they may be the ones to kick the story into motion.

2024's Deadpool & Wolverine was a final hurrah for the FOX X-Men universe, and while the return of many of these characters in Doomsday stole the movie's thunder a bit, it is still a great watch. The film follows Deadpool as he discovers that his Earth is going to be destroyed by the TVA due to his anchor being, Wolverine, dying. So, he goes on a multiversal search for a replacement Wolverine, kicking off a battle between a band of mutant misfits and one of the MCU's most dangerous villains yet. Luckily, fans who have seen the film know that it ends with Deadpool, Wolverine, X-23, and more of their friends gathering around the dinner table. Deadpool & Wolverine is the perfect analogy for many Thanksgivings, as it tells the story of an incredibly stressful experience with a group of people who can't stop butting heads, only for everyone to make up at the table.

Like Tobey Maguire's Spider-Man, Hugh Jackman's Wolverine and Ryan Reynolds' Deadpool aren't confirmed to appear in Avengers: Doomsday . However, Jackman and Reynolds have been credited on the film for contributing literary material. It would be odd for the two actors to only be working on the movie behind the scenes without reprising their iconic superhero roles, meaning that it's likely that they could pop up when Avengers: Doomsday finally hits theaters.

What is your favorite Thanksgiving movie? Let us know on the ComicBook Forum !

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Disney's classic roster of villains have been taking over the anime world in a wild new kind of way, and now fans have gotten a much better look at its Season 2 return with the first full trailer helping to show it all off. Disney Twisted-Wonderland The Animation has been a notable mobile game release where classic Disney Villains get new anime makeovers , and the first season of its official anime adaptation made its debut last year. Now it's coming back for a new season with a new arc on Disney+ next month.

Disney Twisted-Wonderland The Animation Season 2 will be hitting Disney+ on December 23rd, and with it is going to be adapting the Episode of Savanaclaw from the game. Much like how the first season had a school inspired by the Queen of Hearts from Alice in Wonderland , this next season is inspired by Scar from The Lion King . You can check out the new trailer for the coming season below to get an idea of what to expect.

Officially titled as Disney Twisted-Wonderland The Animation ~Episode of Savanaclaw~ , the second season of the series will be making its debut with Disney+ in Japan on December 23rd . International release plans for the anime have yet to be announced as of this time, but it will likely be available for streaming with Hulu and Hulu on Disney+ in the United States when it makes its debut much like the first season. It will be running for eight episodes in total, and has also confirmed that new episodes will be releasing on a weekly basis.

Takahiro Natori returns from the first season to serve as chief director and script supervisor for Disney Twisted-Wonderland The Animation ~Episode of Savanaclaw~ while Shin Katagai serves as director for Yumeta Company and Graphinica. Yoichi Kato provides the scripts for the series, Hanaka Nakano and Akane Sato provide the character designs, and Takumi Ozawa returns from the original mobile game release to compose the music. But it's heading into an entirely different arc with the focus on a different school than seen in the first season.

Disney Twisted-Wonderland The Animation was originally announced with a three arc adaptation with the intent of adapting the Episode of Heartslabyul (as seen with the first season), Episode of Savanaclaw (as seen in this new season), and Episode of Octavinelle arcs from the mobile game release. The main voice cast from the first season are set to reprise their respective roles, but there will be more of a focus on the Savanaclaw students seen prior such as Yuichiro Umehara as Leona Kingscholar, Taito Ban as Jack Howl, and Aoi Ichikawa as Ruggie Bucchi.

There will be a new main protagonist at the center of the second season too with Fairouz Ai as Yuuka Hirasaka, a Judo student who ends up whisked away to this titular wonderland. So it's got an extra bit of fun for those Isekai fans hoping to scratch that kind of anime itch as well along with adding that bump from Disney icons. But how are you liking Disney Twisted-Wonderland The Animation so far? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.

articles.title: Why Mike Flanagan Just Couldn't Kill Carrie White
articles.summary: Flipping the script from Stephen King's novel and Brian De Palma's film, the 'Carrie' showrunner always knew his version of the iconic character would meet a different fate — even if there was no season two.
articles.content:
Mike Flanagan 's Carrie , released on Prime Video last month, has been an all-around success. It scored a second season, bringing the story past what those might remember from the Stephen King novel and the 1976 Brian De Palma film. Flanagan's most excited for the show's lead, Summer H. Howell, and the rest of the cast.

"Watching the ascension of Summer Howell in real time has been incredible. And I've been waiting to see the rest of the world catch up with Samantha Sloyan for a long time now," he tells The Hollywood Reporter over Zoom. "That's been really exciting." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories TV 2026 International Emmy Winners Revealed: 'Carême' Wins Best Drama Business Bela Bajaria Calls Time at Netflix a "Fun Chapter" as She Teases Rest and "Conversations" in First Remarks on Exit

The showrunner is already gearing up for more, sitting for a conversation in his office earlier this month. He's back in the writers room and ready to make more of the show after spending some time "unofficially" working on it before it was picked up for the second season. "We're right into season two, so now the time to enjoy it is over," Flanagan says. "I'm back to work."

Below, the writer digs into what it was like to make his version of the iconic prom scene, whether he's changed his mind on the direction of the story and why he just couldn't kill off Carrie White.

I spoke with Summer for our Next Big Thing series , and one thing she said to me that stuck out was that you told her Carrie was as much hers as it was yours or Stephen [King]'s. How did you get that across?

It's a daunting thing for anyone to step into a legacy of any size, but especially one as monolithic as Carrie White. It's an intimidation that I certainly felt very acutely going into it, and I really didn't want Summer in particular, but any of our actors to have to shoulder. There's so much pressure when you know you are inhabiting a character that's been portrayed as iconically as Carrie White. It's unavoidable. It was very fortunate that Summer had never seen DePalma's film and had never seen Sissy Spacek's incredible performance. I loved that. I really didn't want to change that because I think [it's] the only way to get through a situation that can be so fraught with pressure and anxiety and insecurity and second-guessing yourself and constantly trying to toe the line between invention and the courage we ask of actors in roles like this against the history of the part and the public perception and everything else. The only way she could make it through that was if she truly had an enormous amount of agency within the character and if it became hers. We didn't want to see Summer's interpretation of or homage to Sissy's performance. We wanted to see Summer's Carrie. That was something that was really important to me, and I think ultimately to Summer as well. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

To that point, she mentioned that you made it a point to hire several women to help shape this narrative. Why was that important to you?

It's a story about what it means to be a young woman in a world that fears and misunderstands them. [It's] about the journey between girlhood and adolescence and young womanhood. I don't know what the hell I'm talking about, as much as I want to. I want to understand that. But I think a big thing for me was just being able to say, "I don't know this world. I can't speak about it with any authority, and the only way this is going to work is if I surround myself with people who do know what they're talking about and hand them the keys to the show." It's something we do for all of our shows, whatever the show happens to be about. There may be, at times, a temptation for creatives to feel like because we've been entrusted with a project, we must be an expert on it. Time and time again, in my experience, that hasn't been true. It's an inherently and undeniably female story, and it needed inherently and undeniably brilliant women to tell it and to bring it to life. It was a great honor for me to be able to empower them as much as I possibly could.

How's everything going with season two? Where are you in the process?

I turned in the first episode script earlier this morning, which is very exciting. We've been working on it unofficially for a while because I had always hoped that it could go this way and wanted to be prepared in case it did. We're gearing up to hopefully go into production next year, and we'll see how it all shapes up. The beautiful thing is that Carrie's journey has always seemed to me to have a clear trajectory. And that was something, even though we were never taking for granted that it would happen, it was something that was always in the back of my mind. I know it was in conversations that I had with Summer about where she could go and with Steve too — King was very aware and excited about the potential for that. It's always been in the room with us, but we didn't really have permission to fully explore it until it was real because you don't want to jinx it. But we are fully immersed in it. The writers room is firing on all cylinders. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

How long into developing the take did you make the conscious decision to change the ending and decide you wanted it to continue? Was that always the intention, or did it happen organically?

It happened organically in breaking that first season, in contemplating this very different version of who Carrie White was. She's a very different character than she's ever been. That character — starting her from a place of such kind of wide-eyed innocence and this core of her that's so earnest and eager and kind and curious about the world. It broke my heart to imagine a version of the story that she didn't survive. The first time I came back and said, "Well, here's what I see for a season of Carrie — if it were going to be a limited series, here's how I would see it." Even then, it felt right to me that she survived the story and go out into the world. I thought she'd earned it. Whether we'd ever follow her into that world was the open question, but we'd see her go. That was always part of the pitch for it. It's nice to say there's potential in a story for the audience to get to continue on the road with the character, but it felt to me that this particular incarnation of the character — I didn't want to live in a world where she died at the end of it.

This is a very different version of Carrie White than we've seen before.

The point of the story was different and killing her at the end, or even just reducing her to a killer at the end, really worked against the purpose of the story for us, and the purpose of the story that Steve was excited about too. The revenge tragedy version of it, we thought, had already been told beautifully and exists in amber forever. What excited me, Steve and Summer, as we got into it, was [that] we're telling a different story. As we're talking about cruelty and school violence and reconciling that tug of war in each of us between empathy and kindness and cruelty, what is the message we're leaving people with about this? The message of kill your tormentors and then be dead. It just doesn't feel like the story we're telling. It feels like a horrible message to put into the world, today especially. All of us, Stephen King included, were very committed to a different road for this. It had a different heart to it by the end of it. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

You've previously said you had envisioned this as a three-part story, so presumably three seasons. Do you still feel that way now that you're into season two?

I do. I do. There's a very clean arc. I can see it as a beginning, a middle and an end. The danger's in the temptation to do more, which is very presumptuous because right now we only know we're doing two. That hasn't changed for me at all. It feels like a really clean arc.

There is, understandably, always temptation when things are doing well to do more, but there is a beauty in being able to know when it's OK to stop.

Television is rife with examples of people who fell victim to that temptation and then had to tread water and do jazz hands beyond the expiration point or to stretch it. There's so many clear examples of that. They're wonderful cautionary tales for us.

I can't think of a moment more etched in pop culture stone than the Carrie prom scene. How did you approach your take on the sequence?

One of the most daunting sequences of my career. Twofold. One was I knew when I agreed to do the project, and when we were going to move forward, I was like, well, I have to do the prom. I have to do that myself. If we're going to do Carrie , you got to do the prom. The logistics of the scene, it is the most complex sequence of my career.

The shot list for the prom, which starts in episode seven and doesn't end until halfway through episode eight — just the shot list is so much more voluminous than the script. It's this huge document, and it's logistically enormously complicated. We're tying up the arcs of so many principal characters and so many perspectives. There's extras and stunts and fire and water and blood and effects and everything. We're destroying a set as we go through it, so we have to make sure we're very deliberate about that. We're stepping into the shadow of one of the most iconic sequences in genre filmmaking history. DePalma's aesthetic approach to the prom is legendary and full of things that are so, like you said, burned into pop culture that we have to actively avoid them in something like this. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid4' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

People asked if we were going to do split screens. [I said], "Hell no. We're not going to do anything that's going to come anywhere near the aesthetic approach that has come before it. There's no point. It's done perfectly." In the middle of all of that, which was incredibly stressful and huge, I do remember on the second day that we were shooting it… It took us 10 days to film it. It was a lot of work. I was sitting on the stage in the gym and looking out — Summer was over there in her dress and everybody was in place and everything was going on. It occurred to me that I was at the prom with Carrie White, and that's another feeling that comes out of the fact that this is so ingrained in our consciousness.

I remember grabbing the AD's microphone and encouraging everybody to put the work down. Just for a minute, put everything down, take a breath, forget about the rush we're under, take a breath and look around at each other. Everybody take a moment and realize we're all at the prom with Carrie and just mark the moment a little. Then, from there, [we] went into days and days [of shooting]. We were shooting on a stage, [so] there's no daylight. We don't know what time it is. It's just an endless prom that starts with music and dancing and joy and Summer's up there beaming. By the end of it, we're all covered with blood and smoke and flames and water and all of it's happening to us as a crew while we dismantle and destroy this world that we've spent six months building. It was an incredible experience to shoot it. It's one of my favorite sequences of my career and absolutely the most difficult.

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Avengers: Doomsday hits theaters in just a few weeks, and although anticipation is growing within the fanbase, the release of the final trailer has some concerned about a major issue with the plot. Yesterday's trailer came with a whole host of reveals, including, among other things, that Steve Rogers and Peggy Carter have son (who looks to be about pre-teen age, but that's not been clarified yet), that Steve and Bucky will finally be reunited , and seemingly that the theory that Steve is really Loki is wrong .

If that's sound like a lot of Steve Rogers, that's because it is. A surprising amount of the trailer was focused on Steve, which comes on the heels of Steve's Doomsday arc being teased in the bonus footage of Avengers: Endgame Encore , with Loki showing up to Steve and Peggy's house, likely to address the fact that Steve's decision to stay in the past and live out a married life with Peggy was the cause of Doomsday . Yet, some fans are taking significant issue with this emphasis on Steve, and it extends beyond just Doomsday , into a reflection of the Multiverse Saga as a whole.

Steve Rogers Was Absent in the Multiverse Saga, And Now He's a Central Figure If you felt very little (or perhaps nothing) with the reveal of Steve Rogers' son in the most recent Doomsday trailer, you wouldn't be alone, and that doesn't necessarily have anything to do with the frustrations over Steve's actions apparently causing Doomsday . Rather, it's simply difficult to feel emotionally affected by a reveal such as this one, considering that Steve hasn't been in an MCU project since Endgame seven years ago. With so much time away, audiences just may not have that same emotional investment, and that spells larger trouble because it seems as though Doomsday will be centering Steve as the emotional core of the movie. Yet, audiences are asking how that can be true when he hasn't even been around in years.

That is my problem with it https://t.co/FFEHn8NKDP

Presumably, Marvel wanted the return of Chris Evans/Steve Rogers to feel like a momentous occasion and, when it was first announced, a massive reveal, and perhaps that necessitated Steve not appearing at any point the Multiverse Saga. The trouble is that this gives Steve loose connections at best to what is happening, and that only reinforces the concerns that many fans had about Doomsday feeling disjointed or out of left field (something that also seems troubling in light of Thor's unfortunate line in the final Doomsday trailer , in which he admits he doesn't know half of the heroes present or what they do).

Now the question simply remains: can Doomsday effectively get audiences reinvested in Steve's story quickly enough to make the movie work? If the movie is only banking on viewers still caring about Steve from Endgame and earlier, it might find itself in some hot water. For now, audiences just have to wait and see.

Are you invested in Steve's story in Doomsday , or do you wish the focus was somewhere else? Let us know in the comment down below.

articles.title: One Hunger Games Star Turned Down Their Role Multiple Times: “I Didn't Think There Was Enough To Do”
articles.summary: Woody Harrelson turned down the role of Haymitch Abernathy in The Hunger Games twice before director Gary Ross convinced him to take the part. The actor had read Suzanne Collins’ books and liked them but wasn't convinced there was enough for him to do as Katniss Everdeen’s mentor. Fourteen years later, Harrelson is watching another […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Woody Harrelson turned down the role of Haymitch Abernathy in The Hunger Games twice before director Gary Ross convinced him to take the part. The actor had read Suzanne Collins’ books and liked them but wasn't convinced there was enough for him to do as Katniss Everdeen’s mentor. Fourteen years later, Harrelson is watching another actor take on the role of Haymitch in a movie built entirely around the character, The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping .

Harrelson discussed his initial reservations about joining the franchise in a conversation with his successor, Joseph Zada, for Vanity Fair . "I thought it was good, I read the books, really good, but I just don’t think there’s enough to do. I don’t know if there’s enough to do. It’s an arbitrary, odd way of assessing it." The actor admitted that he can't imagine his life without the experience of making the movies and the friendships he formed along the way. Fortunately, Ross wasn't willing to take no for an answer. The director told Harrelson that he didn't have a second choice for Haymitch. After about ten minutes on the phone with Ross, Harrelson agreed to do the movie. He said, "Gary calls me, and he's like, 'Woody, you have to do this part. I don't have a second choice. You have to play Haymitch.’ And he just talked to me for about 10 minutes on the phone. I'm like, 'All right, okay, yeah, let's do it.'"

Harrelson has seen what Zada does with the character in The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping and couldn't be happier with his successor. “I really can't imagine anyone doing a better job,” Harrelson told the young actor. He was particularly impressed with how Zada develops the cynicism that would come to define Haymitch. While audiences were introduced to the character as a hard-drinking, cynical mentor to Katniss and Peeta, Zada has the opportunity to show audiences the young man Haymitch was before the Capitol robbed him of his optimism.

It's somewhat ironic that Harrelson was initially concerned about the size of the role given how much of the larger story of The Hunger Games hinges on Haymitch. He's one of the few characters who understands what Katniss is going through long before she becomes the face of the rebellion. Having survived the Second Quarter Quell , Haymitch knows that winning the Hunger Games doesn't necessarily mean you've beaten the Capitol. That informed Harrelson's performance across four movies, but audiences are only now getting to see how Haymitch learned that lesson.

Haymitch isn't even the only franchise mentor Harrelson has turned down twice. The actor was equally reluctant to play Tobias Beckett, Han Solo's mentor in Solo: A Star Wars Story . In that instance, it was producer Allison Shearmur who convinced Harrelson to take the role. Unfortunately, not every filmmaker has been as persistent with Harrelson as Ross and Shearmur were. Among the roles the actor has expressed regret over passing on are the title character in Jerry Maguire and Harry Dunne in Dumb and Dumber . Harrelson famously told producer James L. Brooks that nobody was going to care about a movie about a sports agent. The role earned Tom Cruise his second Academy Award nomination.

What's remarkable about Collins' Sunrise on the Reaping is how much of the young Haymitch she introduces in the book feels consistent with Harrelson's interpretation of the character. Even without knowing the full extent of Haymitch's history, Harrelson always managed to convey how much the man cared about the kids he was being asked to send to their deaths. Now, thanks to Collins and Zada, audiences have a much better understanding of why. For a character Harrelson initially thought didn't have enough to do, Haymitch has proven to be one of the richest characters in the entire franchise. What role that he passed on do you wish Harrelson had taken? Let us know in the comments.

articles.title: World of Warcraft: Forever's Success Is Staggering, But It Comes With The Same Catches As The Original
articles.summary: Courtesy of Blizzard World of Warcraft: Forever launched in early November 2026 and broke tons of Blizzard records in the process, but the game is starting to run into issues players can't ignore. This MMORPG is an alternate version of the original World of Warcraft, bringing back the original 2004 classic in a way that World of Warcraft: […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google World of Warcraft: Forever launched in early November 2026 and broke tons of Blizzard records in the process, but the game is starting to run into issues players can't ignore. This MMORPG is an alternate version of the original World of Warcraft , bringing back the original 2004 classic in a way that World of Warcraft: Classic doesn't. Separate from the modern versions of what WoW is turning into, yet still included in existing subscriptions to the current game, this redesigned title returns players to a nostalgic gameplay setting, but with all of the same pitfalls of that original design as well.

Some players have realized that World of Warcraft: Forever is more like an expansion to the original than a full redux of the first game, giving players a sandbox much closer to the launch of the original WoW . New zones, raids, races, abilities, combinations, build strategies, and more are available in WoW: Forever , but the game keeps the first WoW MMO's original Level 60 cap among other features exclusive to that version. Now that the game has been out for awhile, players are starting to have strong opinions about balancing, exploits, and other features veteran fans might remember were pivotal talking points of the classic World of Warcraft .

Around 15 million or more characters have been made in World of Warcraft: Forever , within less than a month of the title's release. Currently, WoW: Forever has more players than World of Warcraft has had in the last 15 years, with a higher count of characters than the MMO has kept in a long time. Before this, WoW: Cataclysm was the biggest expansion for the game, but Forever 's numbers are actually closer to the first World of Warcraft 's launch than anything else. The momentum of this game can't be denied, with so many players returning to the world of Azeroth or jumping into it for the first time.

Some of the biggest praise for WoW: Forever comes from the game's classic MMO design, where players are given more opportunities to encounter quests through non-linear exploration. Rather than being funneled into linear questlines and scripted segments, players have a greater amount of goals to pursue based on their curiosity. Instead of the game telling you what to do and where to go, characters can party up and simply gain 10-15 quests at a rapid pace just by interacting with the world. More interesting decision making helps elevate the World of Warcraft: Forever experience, but it isn't without its flaws.

With such an authentic return to form of the original WoW design comes the same problems that forced that game to evolve. Currently, one such problem is the multiple infinite money glitches that players are exploiting to bypass progression and trade, with some players running around with endless cash. Clearing some non-elite enemies in the same location over and over would allow players to loot upwards to 100 raw Gold per hour, farming it endlessly to fetch a king's ransom. While Blizzard has issued bans and trade blocks to certain accounts as a result, these exploits mirror WoW 's issues from back in the early 2000s.

Tedium is also a huge enemy of players in World of Warcraft: Forever , as nostalgic design also brings back less fondly remembered grinding for levels, gear, and other content. Poorly itemized gear was vanilla WoW 's kryptonite at times, along with balancing issues that made class synergy for PvP unbearable. To that point, WoW: Forever has several balance problems as of this time of writing too, such as the underwhelming lack of strength given to certain classes. The Holy Paladin and healer specs from other archetypes are severely handicapped right now, with healing builds struggling to keep up.

Currently, Blizzard has very few solutions to any of these systemic issues in World of Warcraft: Forever , instead just handing out bans and telling players to pick different builds rather than addressing issues directly. This could be just a problem in timing, as the game is still within its first month of launch, and sweeping balance updates and other changes take time to implement. However, veteran players worry that Blizzard's slow response time to make changes might lead to increasing friction and frustrating in WoW: Forever , causing players to log off. Right now, some of the biggest issues players want addressed fast are:

Should this game sit within the same problems that plagued the 2004 title that took the world by storm, it may suffer a similar fate. Hardcore classic players will always appreciate the oldest version of the MMO, but nostalgia shouldn't blind fans to much-needed changes Blizzard could implement quickly with modern resources. For World of Warcraft: Forever to even surpass the appeal of the original WoW , it will have to tackle problems head-on, using 22 years of hindsight as a guiding light to help players who want the best experience possible.

What kind of changes would you make to World of Warcraft: Forever right now? Let us know in the comments below!

articles.content:
Movie theater owners are hoping for a Thanksgiving box office feast.

Lionsgate's " The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping " is poised to dominate over the holiday with projections of $80 million to $90 million between Wednesday and Sunday. That's after the dystopian prequel launched last weekend to $120 million, registering as the fifth-largest domestic debut of the year. "Sunrise on the Reaping" will tower over two newcomers, Universal's family comedy "Focker In-Law" and Disney's animated " Hexed ," each of which land in roughly 3,500 theaters on Wednesday and are aiming for $40 million to $45 million over the five-day frame. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Taylor Swift's CMA Return Helped Disney Sell More Ads Taylor Swift Ties Grammy Record for Consecutive Album of the Year Nominations

Meanwhile, the Angel Studios biopic "Hershey," about the foundation of the chocolate empire, is projecting a $6 million to $8 million start over four days and Netflix's Brad Pitt-led "The Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth," a sequel to Sony's "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood," is targeting single digits from 250 Imax screens in North America.

This crop of offerings won't establish a Thanksgiving box office benchmark, though cinema operators are encouraged by the range of offerings. (Plus, domestic ticket sales are already 20% above the same point in 2025 as the box office prepares to surpass $10 billion for the first time since Covid upended the theatrical business). Thanksgiving 2024 was the holiday's biggest on record with $422 million across all films, led by "Moana 2″ ($225 million debut), “Wicked” ($118 million) and “Gladiator II” ($44 million). Other top Turkey Days were 2018 with $315 million, fueled by “Ralph Breaks the Internet,” “Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes of Grindelwald” and “Creed II," 2014 with $294 million, powered by “The Hunger Games: Catching Fire," and 2025 with $293 million, boosted by "Zootopia 2" and "Wicked: For Good." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"Hexed" cost above $200 million to produce, not including the many millions spent on global marketing efforts. Since theater owners keep roughly half of ticket sales, Disney needs "Hexed" to resonate outside of the U.S. — and through the holiday season — to justify the massive price tag. While Disney's animated sequels like "Moana 2" and "Zootopia 2" are among the biggest Thanksgiving releases of all time, the studio has struggled with original fare, such as 2024's "Wish" ($31 million over its first five days) and 2022's "Strange World" ($18 million debut over its first five days). Word of mouth will factor into the box office longevity of "Hexed," which follows a teen girl who discovers magical powers that take her from suburbia to Hexe, the world of witches.

"Focker-In-Law" was made for $90 million, a substantial budget given the reality that comedies are a theatrical rarity. (Universal and Paramount co-financed the film.) However, the studios were willing to spend because the three prior films in the "Focker" universe were major box office winners. "Meet the Parents," which debuted 26 years ago and starred Ben Stiller and Robert De Niro as mismatched in-laws Greg Focker and Jack Byrnes, generated $330 million worldwide and inspired two commercially successful sequels, 2004’s “Meet the Fockers” ($522 million worldwide) and 2010’s “Little Fockers" ($310 million worldwide).

In the original, Stiller plays a hapless nurse who endures all kinds of chaos when he's introduced to his girlfriend's family. This time around, Stiller's Greg Focker is the patriarch as his son brings home a new no-nonsense girlfriend, portrayed by Ariana Grande. If "Focker-In-Law" exceeds theatrical expectations, Grande could cement herself as queen of the Thanksgiving box office. This is her third consecutive Turkey Day release following 2024's "Wicked" and 2025's "Wicked: For Good."

articles.title: We Already Know What Marvel's Ghost Rider Sequel Should Be, And It's a Major MCU Crossover
articles.summary: Spider-Man: Brand New Day proved that Marvel doesn’t need to gather the Avengers to stage a major crossover. Spider-Man, the Hulk, and the Punisher all brought three very different superhero archetypes together in one movie. With Ryan Gosling’s Ghost Rider coming in 2028, Marvel already has another unlikely trio from the comics waiting for a […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Spider-Man: Brand New Day proved that Marvel doesn’t need to gather the Avengers to stage a major crossover. Spider-Man, the Hulk, and the Punisher all brought three very different superhero archetypes together in one movie. With Ryan Gosling’s Ghost Rider coming in 2028, Marvel already has another unlikely trio from the comics waiting for a supernatural team-up on screen. The Spirit of Vengeance has a long road to hell ahead of him, but one of his adventures should unite three of Marvel’s most violent antiheroes.

Blackheart is the demon son of Mephisto and is an obvious villain for a Ghost Rider film. His daddy issues were on full display in Nicolas Cage's version when Wes Bentley portrayed the hellspawn. He’s basically the Loki of the Marvel supernatural universe, whose ambitions often bring together heroes to oppose him. With all of the Ghost Rider villains we haven't seen on screen, save Blackheart for the sequel this time around. And let Wolverine and Jon Bernthal’s Punisher come along for the ride. That’s the premise of 1991’s Ghost Rider/Wolverine/Punisher: Hearts of Darkness , a crossover that could give Marvel its next big team-up movie outside the Avengers.

In 1988, Marvel began publishing Marvel Comics Presents , a biweekly anthology that included original adventures outside of the characters' regular titles. Wolverine was practically its mascot, appearing in over 100 straight issues. That included Barry Windsor-Smith’s Weapon X in #72-84, which showed the horrific experiments that bonded adamantium to Logan’s skeleton. Then Ghost Rider joined the party. The #90 issue started the anthology as a flipbook, Wolverine on one cover and Ghost Rider on the other. In issue #100, they teamed up with Doctor Doom to battle Nightmare. The Punisher also showed up in a few issues, including #59 and #101.

Writer Howard Mackie and artist John Romita Jr. united the trio in 1991 for Hearts of Darkness . The oversized comic features Danny Ketch, Logan, and Frank Castle heading to Christ's Crown, a small town under the influence of Blackheart. He has promised each of them information they desperately want, but the demon has another offer. He needs their help to overthrow his father, Mephisto.

Blackheart believes he has three ready accomplices. Wolverine wrestles with his killer instincts. For Frank Castle, killing criminals is his life’s work. Ghost Rider literally rides around and punishes sinners. They're not exactly Boy Scouts, and Blackheart thinks he can use their violent tendencies to his own ends. When they refuse his offer, he takes a young girl named Lucy hostage, forcing the three into a confrontation that ends with Mephisto stepping in.

Blackheart was created by Romita Jr. and Ann Nocenti in Daredevil #270, two years before Hearts of Darkness . The crossover led to a sequel, 1994's The Dark Design , written by Mackie with art by Ron Garney. Back in Christ's Crown, Blackheart returns with an army of corrupted townspeople, forcing Ghost Rider, Wolverine, and the Punisher to team up once more to protect Lucy. The demon kills Mephisto and takes the throne of Hell. Children can be very ungrateful.

From the first time he brought the Avengers together in both the comics and films, Loki has been causing problems that have forced multiple superheroes to come together to stop his machinations. Blackheart could fill a similar role for Marvel’s supernatural characters. He’s strong enough to face off against Ghost Rider, manipulative enough to take advantage of Wolverine, and ambitious enough to threaten Mephisto himself. His schemes give heroes who would otherwise have no reason to work together a reason to do so. Instead of a one-and-done enemy, Blackheart could be a recurring antagonist and return with ever more ambitious schemes, throwing different combinations of Marvel characters into unlikely alliances. The Dark Design could be the supernatural MCU's Infinity War , with Blackheart succeeding in overthrowing his father.

Brand New Day showed what a blast these smaller crossovers could be. We could have Wolverine and The Punisher in Ghost Rider’s world, and it wouldn’t detract from Ghost Rider’s movie. Hulk and Punisher shared Spider-Man’s adventure. Christ’s Crown isn’t your usual MCU battleground, it’s got demons, possessed townsfolk, and three heroes who’d probably rather fight alone. Marvel has spent decades pairing unlikely characters to take on Blackheart . Hearts of Darkness offers a ready-made Ghost Rider sequel and a way to make the villain a recurring threat throughout the supernatural MCU.

Also, Ghost Rider and Wolverine already ride motorcycles. And if Jeremy Allen White ends up being Wolverine , we know he can handle a bike. Dolph Lundgren's Frank Castle rode one. Let's see if Jon Bernthal can handle a chopper too. What would these three even name their motorcycle club? Let us know in the comments.

articles.content:
Jason Segel ( Shrinking , The Muppets , Forgetting Sarah Marshall ) has joined the Oscar-qualified short film Meeting Your Maker as an executive producer. Written and directed by Gregory J.M. Kasunich, the heartfelt 18-minute dark comedy film follows Otis, a beloved children’s TV puppet who, following a suicide attempt, awakens in a workshop and must confront his creator. Otis must grapple with questions of identity, purpose, and what it means to be alive. The film stars Jonathan Kite ( 2 Broke Girls ) alongside Thomas Lennon, Amanda Maddock, Jason and Randy Sklar, Lenny Jacobson, Anna Chazelle, Kayla Radomski, Dylan Playfair, Dylan Mooney, Victor Yerrid and Darcy Rose Byrnes. The 18-minute short was produced by Derek Tramont and Lee Sacks. Segel has explored similar emotional territory throughout his career, from his work writing and starring in The Muppets to his performance in the Apple TV+ hit series Shrinking . Blending practical puppetry, surreal production design, and an ensemble of comedic performers, Meeting Your Maker explores the complicated relationship between artists and their creations, asking what happens when the character you’ve spent your life bringing to life begins to question their own existence.

"There’s something really special about Meeting Your Maker ," said Segel. "It has this wonderful balance of comedy and heartbreak, this sort of magical melancholy that I’ve always been drawn to. It makes you laugh, and then, almost without realizing it, you find yourself thinking about some pretty big questions like who we are, what gives our lives meaning, and what happens when we lose sight of our purpose." Added Segel: "I’ve always believed that puppetry has this incredible ability to make us feel things we might otherwise be afraid to confront. There’s something about that innocence and imagination that allows us to be a little more honest with ourselves. And I think that’s especially important right now, when so many people are struggling to feel seen or connected. What Gregory has created is funny, strange, and ultimately hopeful. It reminds us that even in our darkest moments, there’s still room for laughter, connection, and magic. articles.title: I Wondered Why Marvel Dropped Those Four Avengers: Doomsday Teasers So Early. Joe Russo Explained
articles.summary: Those clips came surprisingly early.
articles.content:
Fans who spent years watching the Marvel movies in order are gearing up for the shared universe's next big crossover event with Avengers: Doomsday . Arguably the most anticipated upcoming Marvel movie in years, the blockbuster has been steadily building excitement since those teasers arrived back in January . Now Joe Russo explained why they decided to give us footage that early.

Marvel is known for its tight security , so it was surprising that we got footage from Doomsday so many months before the movie's December release. The industry has changed a bit since Endgame arrived in theaters, and the MCU has had a number of box office blunders including bombs like The Marvels . As such, The Russos wanted get the hype train running early, with more news, casting, and footage methodically released to the public.

Those brief clips quickly went viral, especially the Captain America teaser that confirmed Chris Evans was returning as Steve Rogers. With the next Avengers movie now just a few weeks away from its release, anticipation has reached a fever pitch that should (hopefully) result in massive box office numbers. Perhaps future MCU projects will follow this same strategy.

EXCLUSIVE : David Tennant 's cameo at the end of The Four Seasons ' Season 2 finale was more than an amusing callback to the imaginary boyfriend Anne (Kerri Kenney-Silver) had conjured up earlier in the season — a lot more.

While a Season 3 return for Tennant was expected after that cliffhanger, Deadline can reveal that the Doctor Who alum is a series regular on the upcoming installment of the Netflix comedy series, which is now filming.
